h: Queen of the Suburbs, King of the Scoreboard
p: Ealing has long been nicknamed the Queen of the Suburbs, thanks to its leafy streets, grand Victorian houses and village-green feel. It's the sort of place where Sunday mornings are for long walks and brunch, but on a Friday night the town centre around Ealing Broadway gets properly lively. A games bar here gives west Londoners a good reason not to trek into the West End.

Transport is a big selling point. Ealing Broadway station serves the Central and District lines, the Elizabeth line and National Rail services, so you can get here quickly from central London, Heathrow or further west. That makes it a handy meet-in-the-middle spot for groups scattered across the capital and beyond.

For the best night, book your games before you arrive and give everyone a time to aim for. Split into teams that mix the confident with the shy, and keep the scores on show for maximum bragging rights. If you're celebrating, think about building in time for food, so you're not running out of energy halfway through the second game.

Daytime in Ealing is lovely. Ealing Common and the green spaces around the town are perfect for a stroll, and there are plenty of independent cafés and restaurants along the main roads. The famous Ealing comedies were made at the studios on the green, and film fans might enjoy tracking down some of the locations. Further west, Osterley Park and House, with its grand mansion and grounds, is a peaceful escape that still feels like proper countryside.
